_doc: Tuning for the Drift campaign (region_weight: the weight of an event that asks for a region (requires.region) is multiplied by it where it is picked (events.gd pick), so a homeland is felt; measured by the content audit's campaign walk (2026-11-03), about 15% of the draws. scripts/space/drift.gd makes the map, campaign.gd runs it, docs/CONTENT.md section 8). map: the defaults of every region's map (docs/CONTENT.md section 15; a region file may override any of these keys): nodes = how many in all (fixed places included; [least, most] rolls it), size = the region in px, margin = how close to the edge a random node may sit, min_spacing = least distance between two nodes, lane_third and lane_fourth = chance a node asks for a 3rd and a 4th lane (all ask for 2), lane_length = longest lane made for fun (connecting lanes may be longer), clearance = how near a lane may pass another node, clan_trader = chance a trader node is a Scrapper one. node_weights: the type of every non-fixed node is rolled by these (a region's own node_weights replace them). types: label, colour and glyph the map draws (`exit` is a region's exit beacon). The fixed places are in the region files (data/regions/*.json, places: pos in px; jitter = seeded wobble; faction = who runs it; hidden_until = a flag that must be set before the node shows; beacon = always on the map; start = where the region begins). run (scripts/space/regions.gd): a run crosses `stages` regions; stage 1 is `start`; the exit beacon of every stage offers `offers` [least, most] regions valid for the next stage (rolled by their weight times the `rarity` factor, never one already visited), the last stage's exit leads to the `ending` region (which has no exit); `entry` is the arrival node added to a region with no start place, `exit` its exit beacon (far side). fuel (playtest 2, economy: fuel is scarce): the item `fuel` costs `price` credits at stations, a drift jump costs `drift_hull` hull integrity. Only the places in `stations` (about 70% of them: 13 of 33 at first, 20 and then 24 since the progression audit, the regions of stages 3 to 8 first and then the common ones of stages 2 to 7: a region's own station, the one a run needs to cross it) sell fuel at all (campaign.gd adds the service; the `services` of a menu below do not list it, and the Scrapper trader never sells it), and a visit has only `stock` [least, most] units on sale ([2, 4], then [4, 8] and since the second pass of the progression audit [6, 10]: its bot makes 11 to 15 jumps a stage, not the 8 this was first sized for, and at [4, 8] it still drifted 3 jumps a stage), rolled from the run's seed, the station and the visit, refilled by the next visit (campaign.gd fuel_left). `start` is the least fuel a run begins with (run_start.gd fuel_up tops the ship's cargo up to it; it was 6, then the stations, the traders and the canisters were cut and tests/tool_fuel_rate.gd, which plays 100 seeded runs, found 22 the tank at which about one run in five needs the tow). A normal jump takes 1 fuel times the thrust-weighted mean `fuel_mult` of the powered engines (campaign.gd jump_cost; the fraction is kept and paid in whole fuel). danger: jumps at which the enemy tier goes up. enemies: the enemy of a fight by kind and tier: a design file (a path), or a generated ship (scripts/space/shipgen.gd, data/enemy_tables.json): gen: takes the faction the region of the node meets in such a fight, gen:<faction> names one, and :ram after it makes it a ram-bowed rammer. The fixed designs (pirate_raider, rustfang_rammer) stay available by id. loot: after a won fight, the credits range (times the tier; x1.5 for a captured ship); the salvage pick of the surviving parts is scripts/space/salvage.gd, whose Scan row offers the unknown recipe of an offered part that the ship can craft next (Salvage.next_recipe: its level at most the fabricator's + 1, its tool known or on the fabricator; fabricator modules first, then core weapons and shields, then racial ones, then other parts without the top tier; a boarding's blueprint is the same pick) (threat_picks: the extra parts it offers after an enemy of 4 or 5 skulls of threat, by skulls); drone_scan: the chance that a salvage also offers a row to scan the Repair Drone blueprint while it is unknown, rolled from the run's seed and the fights won, so the campaign's rng is left alone, and its strip row (a won fight) or the scrap paid for a captured ship is (strip_base + strip_per_part x the enemy's parts left) x the tier. prices: hull repair per point, the fraction of value paid when selling, the recruit price, how many recruits a station offers when it has any, and recruit_chance (the chance a station has anyone to hire on a visit). crew (playtest 2, A2: crew are rare): a gate on events that add crew, applied where an event is picked (events.gd crew_factor): the chance an eligible event that adds crew is in the pool at all: unique_event for one that brings a unique character, station_event for a station greeting that brings an ordinary recruit, species_event for any other such event (Ada's event is not gated); measure with tests/tool_crew_rate.gd. values: what things are worth (sale = half): per material rarity, per component tier, unique parts, and per item kind. stations: the menu of each place (services: sell, stock, repair, recruit, and fuel for the places listed in `fuel.stations`; stock = id -> price; recruit = species -> weight; faction decides refusal and discounts). Engine prices (engine wave 1, nothing of tier 4 or 5 is ever sold): the Mk1 price of the part's line (Kickjet 90, Concord Thruster 120, Ion Drive 300) times the part value of its tier over that of tier 1 (values.tier: 40, 90, 160), rounded to 10; Strafe Jets cost half of the Concord Thruster of their tier (half the recipe), a Long-Burn Drive the same as one. `clan_trader` is the menu of a Scrapper trader node. instant_jump: true keeps the beta's jump (clicking a node jumps at once); false makes a jump a spool (jump.spool seconds of charge, campaign.gd start_jump and tick_jump) that waits while a hostile is within jump.hostile_range px, with the sector flow of docs/CONTENT.md section 11.

events._doc: Event memory (events.gd fade_weight): every time an event is shown in a run (campaign.story_views counts every id; a pick through Events.pick: map nodes, docks, people, sites, expeditions) its weight is multiplied by repeat_fade, never under 0.01 so a lone event stays pickable. A heavy once story event keeps its own halving.

shops._doc: Small shops (playtest 2, economy; scripts/space/shops.gd, campaign.gd shop_cfg): the Trader and Store POIs of a sector (data/sectors.json poi_types with shop: true) open a small shop after their event instead of a station menu: a handful of items, some of which no station of the region sells. Each shop is rolled once from the run's seed, its POI and its region (the same shop whenever it is asked for), and what is bought leaves it (campaign.gd shop_sold, saved). items: how many things a shop carries [least, most]; unique: how many of those are from the unique pool [least, most], the rest come from `common` (id -> price, the staples the stations sell too). The unique pool, by kind: racial (every part of the tech_* packs), tier (any other non-unique part of tier `tier_range`; nothing of tier 4 or 5 is ever sold), material (`materials`: id -> price a unit, `material_qty` units on the shelf), drone (`drone`: id -> price), mod and mod1 (`mods`: the boarding mods of data/mods.json, id -> price by tier; `mod1` is the three Mk I ones and rolls three times as often as `mod`, the Mk II and III) and blueprint (`blueprints`: recipe id -> price, a blueprint is sold as the item bp:<recipe id> and learned at once); `kinds` is the weight of each kind in the roll. A part in the pool is priced `part_price` x its value (values.tier, or values.unique), rounded to 5: dearer than a station sells the same. A shop never offers as unique anything the station of its own region sells (a Fenn part in the Fenn Bazaar is no find there); rare materials, blueprints and the parts no station stocks are in no station's stock anywhere. The shop panel marks the unique items RARE.
